candidate.answerReason: Ordered pairs of individual balls give four favorable outcomes out of nine with replacement and two out of six without replacement.

methods.label: Count ordered ball pairs
methods.explanation: (1) With replacement: there are \(3\times3=9\) outcomes in total, and \(2\times2=4\) outcomes in which both draws are red, so the probability is 4/9. (2) Without replacement: there are \(3\times2=6\) outcomes in total, and \(2\times1=2\) outcomes in which both draws are red, so the probability is \(2/6=1/3\).
methods.levelReason: Counting two-stage pairings and reducing the resulting fractions fit the Grade 9 treatment of replacement experiments.
